name: com.reguweb/accessibility
title: Reguweb Accessibility Checker
description: Free WCAG 2.2 accessibility and AI-visibility checks for any web page. No account needed.

tools.name: scan_url
tools.description:
Start a free WCAG accessibility and SEO scan of one public web page. Use this when someone wants to know whether a website is accessible, has WCAG/ADA issues or what its accessibility score is.
The scan runs in the background and takes about 30-90 seconds. This tool returns a scan token straight away: call get_scan_result with that token to read the results.

url.description: The public page to scan, for example "https://example.com" or "example.com/pricing".

tools.name: get_scan_result
tools.description:
Read the results of a scan started with scan_url or check_ai_visibility, using the token that tool returned.
If the status is "queued" or "running", wait about 15 seconds and call this tool again. Results are kept for 7 days.
When you show the results, include the report_url so the person can open the full report.

token.description: The token returned by scan_url or check_ai_visibility.

tools.name: check_ai_visibility
tools.description:
Start a free check of how well AI assistants and AI search engines (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity) can find, read and cite a website: robots.txt rules for AI crawlers, llms.txt, structured data and similar signals.
The check runs in the background and takes about 30 seconds. This tool returns a token straight away: call get_scan_result with that token to read the results.

url.description: The website to check, for example "https://example.com".

tools.name: explain_wcag_criterion
tools.description:
Explain a WCAG 2.2 Level A or AA success criterion in plain English, with how to test for it and a link to the official W3C explanation.
Look it up by number (for example "1.4.3") or by a word from its topic (for example "contrast", "keyboard", "captions", "target size").

criterion.description: A criterion number such as "1.4.3", or a topic word such as "contrast".
